The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident.
2. The claimant is 16 years old and he was a student as on the date of the accident.

Because of the accident, he sustained the following injuries:
1. Multiple abrasion over the face with left peri orbital swelling and discoloration of left eye lid 2. Abrasion over the right clavicle 3. CLW over the left upper lip 4. 7. Right clavicular fracture X-ray and CT scans shown :
Fracture of left humerus, Fracture of right femur, Fracture of right clavicle, Vascular insufficiency in right upper limb.
Amputation of right upper limb.
Because of the said injuries, his right upper limb has been amputated.
There is small stump about 7 to 8 cm in the upper limb.
Claimant has also suffered fracture injury to right femur.
He was hospitalized for a period of 18 days.
As per the evidence of the doctor, he required a prosthesis, which cost about an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- and it may have to be replaced every five years.

3. As per the evidence of the doctor, the claimant sustained 90% disability, however, the Court below had considered 80% disability to the whole body and NC: 2023:KHC:41499 considered the income at Rs.10,000/- per month and granted an amount of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering, an amount of Rs.7,28,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.30,000/-, Rs.10,000/-,
Rs.17,28,000/-, Rs.25,000/-, Rs.1,05,000/-, Rs.25,000, Rs.25,000/-, Rs.20,000/- and Rs.1,00,000/-, conveyance charges, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities, for Prosthesis, loss of marriage prospectus, set back in studies, loss of income and inconvenience to his parents and future medical expenses respectively.
Altogether, the Court below had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.28,96,000/-.

4. In the cross-objection, it is stated by the learned counsel for the claimant that for the injuries and amputation sustained by the claimant, under the head of pain and suffering, granting an amount of Rs.75,000/- is on the lower side.
He submits that the Court below, under the head loss of future income, had not granted a reasonable amount.

He further submits that under the NC:
2023:KHC:41499 head of loss of amenities, only an amount of Rs.25,000/- has been granted, which is on the lower side.

For prosthesis, as per the evidence of the doctor, it requires Rs.2,50,000/-,
however, the Court has granted an amount of Rs.1,05,000/-.
Even under the head loss of marriage prospects, granting an amount of Rs.25,000/- is on the lower side.
It is submitted that the compensation of an amount of Rs.28,96,000/- granted by the Tribunal is not just and reasonable.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the doctor's evidence is that the claimant was suffering from permanent disability of 15.3% to his right lower limb and overall disability of 35.1% to whole body.
The Court below had taken 80% disability which is on the higher side.

He further submits that when the Court below had already granted compensation under the head of loss of future income, again the claimant is not entitled for compensation under the head of disability.

It is submitted that even for prosthesis also, the doctor had NC: 2023:KHC:41499 stated that it would cost an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- and no bills were marked and the Court below failed to consider the said aspect and granted an amount of Rs.1,05,000/-.
It is submitted that under the head of set back in studies also without any evidence, the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.25,000/- which is without any basis.

Learned counsel submits that when the doctor had stated that the future medical expenses would be an amount of Rs.60,000/- the Court below had granted T John Rohit vs The New India Assurance Co.Ltd on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121146107/
4 an amount of Rs.1,00,000/-.

sentences.text: He further submits that the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
Further, the interest was 9% which is contrary to the settled law.

6. In response to that, learned counsel for claimant submits that apart from stating that the disability is 35.1% to the whole body the doctor stated that since the available stump is devoid of neurological and muscular power, functional disability of right upper limb is 100%.
Learned counsel submits that while assessing the loss of NC: 2023:KHC:41499 future income, the Court below had to look at the functional disability.
When the doctor has opined that it is 100%, the Court below had only taken 80%.

It is further submitted that as far as the prosthesis is concerned, the doctor had given the evidence stating that it requires an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- and every 5 years it has to be replaced and granting an amount of Rs.1,05,000/- is on the lower side.
7. Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
In this case, the upper limb has been amputated, along with the fact that the claimant has suffered several injuries.
Therefore, under the head of pain and suffering, this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.1,00,000/-.

Insofar as medical expenses, nourishment and attendant charges and conveyance charges are concerned, the Tribunal had granted an amount of Rs.7,28,000/-, Rs.30,000/- and Rs.10,000/- respectively, which are reasonable and this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same.
Then coming to the head of loss of future income, this Court is not able to appreciate the contention of learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company.
The Court below had rightly considered 80% and granted compensation.
The Court below had considered the income at Rs.10,000/- per month and granted an amount of Rs.17,28,000/- towards loss of future income to the claimant, who is a student and 16 years old.
Considering the same, this Court is not inclined to enhance the said amount, which is reasonable.

The Court below, having granted the compensation of an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of income and amenities, also granted a compensation of an amount of Rs.25,000/- under the head of disability, which is not correct and this Court is not inclined to grant any compensation under the head of disability.

When it comes to loss of amenities,
this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.60,000/-.
When it comes to prosthesis, the doctor has opined Rs.2,50,000/- is required and it has to be changed every five years.
This - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41499 Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards prosthesis considering the evidence of the doctor.
9. Under the head of setback in studies, as rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company there is no evidence and in fact it is stated that he continued with the studies.
Hence, the claimant is not entitled for compensation under the head of set back and studies.
